title: Avenanti 2012 · parietal and visual active control
citation: Avenanti, A., Annela, L., & Serino, A. (2012). Suppression of premotor cortex disrupts motor coding of peripersonal space. NeuroImage, 63(1), 281–288.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.response: Main trials generate right first dorsal interosseous MEPs rather than manual responses. Separately record whether the participant detects strong palm touches in the intertrial interval.
published_method.analysis: Compare raw peak-to-peak MEP amplitude by session, near/far speaker and pulse delay. The 300 ms near-minus-far index supports the between-experiment comparison.
intervention_sessions: Active tDCS over left posterior parietal cortex
Active tDCS over primary visual cortex

source_provenance.value: Two identical speakers. Spectral recordings checked for equal emitted frequencies.
source_provenance.gap: Original waveform, sample rate and speaker model unspecified.

implementation_gaps: Requires qualified tDCS, participant-specific neuronavigation, motor threshold and single-pulse TMS, time-locked EMG, and calibrated physical loudspeakers. These are laboratory interventions, not executable tactile SOAs.

Original sound file, participant-level stimulation settings/coordinates, trigger calibration and measured event timings are unavailable. A separate intertrial palm touch attention check also needs a qualified route.
Resolve the visual-cortex coordinate sign discrepancy in the published table before preparing the active control setup.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
